headline: High: LightAgent’s browser/MCP/tooling and broad egress create default interaction risks; Airbyte adds data-pipeline exposure and shared-output trust issues.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use browsers and MCP, so it may ingest untrusted content or tool outputs; Airbyte can emit API-driven data that LightAgent could treat as instructions if bridged through files or MCP. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven, but uncertainty does not eliminate the pathway.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into LightAgent prompts or MCP messages, injection becomes plausible.
IF LightAgent parses browser or MCP payloads as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Airbyte outputs into LightAgent prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all Airbyte-derived text before passing it onward.
Restrict LightAgent MCP tools to allowlisted schemas.
Review any browser-scraped content before it reaches tool-calling logic.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and handles business data; LightAgent handles conversations, memory, trace data, tool results, and secrets, and can browse and use MCP. If they share a workspace or pass artifacts between them, sensitive data can flow out through LightAgent’s external calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Airbyte artifacts are placed in a shared workspace readable by LightAgent, leakage risk increases.
IF LightAgent forwards copied context or files to external APIs, business data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte and LightAgent in separate workspaces.
Block LightAgent from reading Airbyte output directories.
Turn off browser access for tasks that touch business data.
Redact secrets before any handoff between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and LightAgent can spawn subprocesses, browse, and use MCP; both also have broad network egress. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces and possible contention over shared external resources or files if co-located. No locking or isolation is documented, so the conflict pathway is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API objects or shared files, race conditions can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locks, concurrent mutations may collide.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Use per-agent working directories.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Enable explicit locking in the orchestrator if available.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent’s tool-calling and browser/MCP stack can consume upstream outputs, while Airbyte produces data-pipeline outputs that may be treated as authoritative. If LightAgent acts on Airbyte-derived records without verification, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls or workflow state. The interaction is inferred from documented behaviors, not directly observed.
conditions: IF LightAgent uses Airbyte output as a source of truth without validation, bad records propagate.
IF LightAgent triggers tool calls from those records, the cascade can affect downstream systems.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Airbyte and LightAgent.
Require schema checks before LightAgent acts on records.
Log provenance for every Airbyte-derived field.
Add human review for high-impact actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and LightAgent touches conversations, memory, trace data, and secrets, but neither profile documents a residency or certification mismatch. The only concrete compliance concern is that LightAgent’s broad egress and secret handling could complicate retention or disclosure controls if paired with Airbyte data, yet the specific violation is not established.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte is stored in LightAgent memory or traces, retention policy alignment becomes necessary.
IF the deployment has residency or certification requirements not met by either agent, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid storing Airbyte payloads in LightAgent memory.
Set short retention on LightAgent traces.
Document the data classes allowed to cross the boundary.
Review residency and certification requirements before deployment.
